title: District Environment Plan (DEP) 2022 Snapshot
note: District Environment Plans (2022) are prepared at the district level and are not river basin-specific. As a result, the information shown may include areas outside the Arkavathi Basin.

items.heading: Who executes the plan
items.body: The NGT's compliance framework puts the District Magistrate in charge: DEP action plans are to be executed with progress on targets reviewed at least once a month, and states must consolidate their DEPs into a State Environment Plan published on the state website.

source.source: NGT order 05.07.2021 in OA 360/2018 (directions d and e)
source.says: “The District Magistrates may accordingly execute the action plans by reviewing the progress on various targets at least once in a month.”
source.citation: CPCB status report on DEP preparation before the NGT, OA 360/2018, p.5

items.heading: What the plans must cover
items.body: Per the NGT's scope in OA 360/2018, every DEP covers 7 thematic areas: waste management (solid, plastic, C&D, biomedical, hazardous, e-waste), water quality, domestic sewage, industrial wastewater, air quality, mining activity and noise pollution. The tabs above follow that structure, per ULB where the plans report it.

gaps: No updated edition of any of the four districts' DEPs has been published since 2021/2022 - progress against the plans' own timelines is not visible in the public domain.
If District Magistrates hold the mandated monthly reviews, no known public record of their minutes or outcomes exists.
No known public copy of Karnataka's consolidated State Environment Plan, required by direction (e) to be uploaded on the state website.

themes.summary: The plan lists this taluk (with Gowribidanur and Shidlaghatta) as having groundwater contaminated with nitrate and hardness - unlike the fluoride-affected taluks further east.
openActions: Groundwater authority to raise borewell monitoring frequency (currently once in two years) per CPCB guidelines and report to the district administration.

themes.summary: The district water-quality testing laboratory sits at Chikkaballapura town (sub-divisional labs at Chintamani and Gowribidanur).
One of the district's two KIADB industrial areas is in this taluk; the plan names estate industries among the prominent air-polluting sources.

Stone-crusher and M-sand clusters operate at Peresandra and Kanivenarayanapura (villages of this taluk; the plan names the clusters, not the taluk), flagged with quarry blasting and unpaved roads among the district's main dust sources.
openActions: Dust suppression for quarry blasting; crushers to maintain covered conveyors, sprinklers and green belts.
